title: Behind the Idea: Arf
summary:
Arf co-founder and CEO Ali Erhat Nalbant on why pre-funding still traps capital in cross-border payments and how on-demand settlement liquidity sets it free.
The post Behind the Idea: Arf appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: Arf co-founder and CEO Ali Erhat Nalbant discussed how traditional pre-funding traps capital in cross-border payments. During a recent discussion, he explained that adopting on-demand settlement liquidity can help free up this trapped capital and improve efficiency for financial transactions globally.

COINPAYMENTS and Motorsport Lab Partner to Bring Digital-Asset Payments to Supercars and Luxury Motorsport Travel
summary:
COINPAYMENTS, a global digital-asset payment infrastructure provider, and Motorsport Lab, an experiential motorsport company creating curated supercar journeys, corporate experiences and brand activations for private clients and global organizations, today announced a partnership bringing digital-asset payments to luxury motorsport and experiential travel.
Through the partnership, Motorsport Lab clients will be able to use digital assets to book select high-value experiences through COINPAYMENTS' integrated payment infrastructure, adding flexibility for an increasingly global client base.
The partnership comes as digital assets and stablecoins play an increasingly prominent role in global commerce. According to industry data, global stablecoin transaction value reached approximately $33 trillion in 2025[1], illustrating the scale of digital assets moving through the global economy.
For businesses serving international and high-value customers, digital-asset infrastructure can simplify cross-border transactions while giving clients greater payment flexibility. Through COINPAYMENTS, Motorsport Lab will be able to accept digital assets through an integrated solution designed for businesses operating across international markets.
Throughout 2027, COINPAYMENTS and Motorsport Lab will collaborate on curated motorsport experiences, client engagement opportunities and  international programs, connecting the digital-asset economy with the global community of supercar and motorsport enthusiasts. The first opportunity for Motorsport Lab clients to book experience with COINPAYMENTS will be the Master Control on Ice: The Ultimate Aston Martin Winter Ice Drive across Germany and Austria.
For over a decade, Motorsport Lab has built relationships across the global supercar and motorsport ecosystem, connecting clients with manufacturers, driving academies, racetracks, Formula 1, private automotive collections, automotive personalities and some of the world's most celebrated motorsport destinations.
Specifically, the company’s programs place guests inside the culture surrounding the cars: journeys through Italy’s Motor Valley, home to Ferrari, Lamborghini and Pagani; British motoring experiences connected to Goodwood and Aston Martin; classic Porsche and modern supercar driving through Barcelona and Catalonia; winter ice driving and drifting in Austria; and Japanese Domestic Market experiences from Tokyo to Hakone incorporating mountain driving, drifting, racetracks and Japan’s distinctive automotive culture.
The collaboration with COINPAYMENTS creates a bridge between these real-world experiences and the rapidly expanding digital-asset economy.
Stacy Belf, Head of Sales, North America at COINPAYMENTS , said: "Today's luxury consumer is increasingly global, entrepreneurial and comfortable holding wealth in digital assets."
"Motorsport Lab operates at the intersection of luxury travel, supercars, Formula 1 and experiential hospitality. Our partnership gives clients greater flexibility in how they transact while creating new opportunities for us to engage with this community through extraordinary real-world experiences."
For Motorsport Lab Founder Ray Chang, the partnership represents the continued evolution of a company he started around a single Ferrari 360 more than a decade ago.
"Our clients aren't simply looking to rent an exotic car or book another luxury vacation. They want access to the culture behind the cars: the factories, people, roads, racing and food, including opportunities to engage with and invest in technologies shaping how we drive, race and connect human and machine," said Ray Chang, Founder of Motorsport Lab.
“For our corporate clients, these experiences can also bring leadership teams together, reward and retain key people, deepen customer relationships, create differentiated content and open doors to new business. In many ways, it’s the next generation of the President’s Club, an alternative to the familiar golf trip or wellness retreat.”
"Whether we're taking guests through Motor Valley in Italy, driving classic Porsches through Catalonia, ice drifting in Austria or creating an experience around Formula 1, these are often significant international purchases. COINPAYMENTS gives our clients a seamless way to turn digital assets into unforgettable real-world experiences."

title: One in Three Younger Workers Fear AI Could Soon Do Their Job Better Than Them
summary:
One in three younger UK workers (33%) worry artificial intelligence could soon do their job better than they can, according to new research from European financial technology provider, payabl.
This compares with just 16% of workers aged 55 and over, revealing a generational divide in how employees view the impact of AI on their working lives. Across the workforce as a whole, more than one in four (26%) say they are worried AI will soon be able to do their job better than they can.
The findings highlight several central challenges facing businesses as AI adoption accelerates: how to use the technology while ensuring employees understand how it will change their roles and equipping them with the skills and confidence to work alongside it.
Jolita Strasunskaite, Group Chief People Officer at payabl., said: “AI is changing work incredibly quickly, and it's understandable that this creates uncertainty. What stands out from our research is that younger workers are among those expressing the greatest concern about what AI could mean for their role.
“Leaders shouldn't dismiss that anxiety, nor should we respond by pretending that jobs and skills won't change. Our responsibility is to give people clarity about how AI is being used, invest in the skills they will need and create an environment where employees see technology as something that can increase their capabilities rather than simply compete with them.
“The organisations that get this right won't necessarily be those that adopt AI fastest. They'll be the ones that bring their people with them.”
Putting people at the centre of AI in payments
The research comes as payabl. returns as Networking Sponsor of the European Women Payments Network (EWPN) Annual Conference 2026, taking place at AI House in Amsterdam on 3 November under the theme, Human-Centric AI and the Future of Payments & Financial Services. 
Merima Mahmutovic, Chair of the Executive Board, EWPN, said: “AI is already rapidly reshaping payments and financial services. This year’s conference is about ensuring that people remain at the centre of that transformation, from how AI is designed and governed to how it informs leadership, work and the customer experience. Bringing together different perspectives from across the industry is critical to that, and payabl.’s continued support helps us create the space for those conversations.”
Strasunskaite will join a roundtable titled ‘The Leadership Playbook for the AI Era’, discussing how leaders bring their people with them as AI transforms financial services. Christia Evagorou, Deputy Group CEO at payabl., will participate in the panel ‘Your Data, Their Model: Who Really Controls the AI Economy?’, exploring the ethics of data use in financial services.
Evagorou said: “Financial institutions hold enormous amounts of information about people's financial lives. As AI becomes more powerful, customers need meaningful transparency about how their information is being used and how it affects decisions made about them. Ultimately, there also needs to be human accountability.”
payabl.'s support for EWPN extends beyond the annual conference. Ugnė Buračienė, Group CEO of payabl., serves as EWPN Country Ambassador for Cyprus, supporting the network's community and mission locally. Strasunskaite will also serve as a judge for the 2026 EWPN Awards, taking place on 2 November ahead of the conference. The awards recognise individuals and organisations making an impact across payments, inclusion, education and community. Nominations are open until 20 October 2026. Submit a nomination for the EWPN Awards 2026.
Strasunskaite added: “Technology is going to change our industry enormously, but technology doesn't decide what kind of industry we build; people do. Who is represented when decisions are made will influence the technology we build, the risks we identify and ultimately who benefits from innovation.”

emerchantpay and LoopingOne Enable Digital Transactions for Motorhome Depot in the UK
summary:
emerchantpay, a leading global payment service provider and acquirer, has partnered with LoopingOne, a deal flow platform for high-value transactions, to enable a fully digital transaction journey for Motorhome Depot, Europe’s largest motorhome marketplace. The collaboration combines LoopingOne’s streamlined marketplace deal flow capabilities with emerchantpay’s payment infrastructure, bringing KYC verification, payment processing and funds settlement into a single digital transaction workflow for Motorhome Depot in the UK.  
 
Motorhome Depot is the first merchant to benefit from the joint offering by emerchantpay and LoopingOne, which is available to businesses and marketplaces in the UK and Europe.   
 
Motorhome Depot connects motorhome sellers with prospective buyers through its nationwide network of brokers. Once a sale has been agreed, brokers can use the LoopingOne platform to manage the transaction digitally, replacing a previous manual payment process with an integrated workflow. emerchantpay provides payment processing services within the LoopingOne platform, while the solution enables funds to be paid out to the seller on the same day following a successful transaction 
 

Sigurdur Gudmundsson, Chief Commercial Officer at emerchantpay, said: “High-value transactions require payment infrastructure that gives every participant confidence while keeping the experience straightforward. Working with LoopingOne and Motorhome Depot demonstrates how a complex deal can be simplified within one digital journey. This solution is an important milestone and establishes a strong foundation for further shared success. We look forward to extending these capabilities to more businesses with complex, high-value transaction requirements.” 
 

Mark van der Suis, Director and Co-founder at LoopingOne, said: “LoopingOne brings the different steps of a high-value transaction together in one digital workflow. By integrating emerchantpay’s payment capabilities into the platform, we can provide Motorhome Depot’s brokers and their customers with a straightforward way to manage the transaction from verification and payment through settlement, while enabling sellers to receive their funds quickly.” 
 

Lucy Garbett, Financial Operations Manager at Motorhome Depot, said: “Buying or selling a motorhome is a significant transaction and we want the process to be as straightforward as possible. Our collaboration with LoopingOne and emerchantpay gives our broker network a single digital environment for transactions and the ability to receive their funds promptly.”

title: PPRO Partners with Damisa for Stablecoin-Powered Treasury and Cross-Border Settlement
summary:
Damisa, the regulated stablecoin-native settlement platform for cross-border business payments, today announced that PPRO, the local payments platform behind global payment service providers and merchants, has partnered with Damisa. What began as a focused deployment in the Latin American region is now scaling with PPRO’s global expansion.
Through the partnership, PPRO taps into Damisa's onramp and off-ramp network to move money. Damisa converts the funds into regulated stablecoins and moves them across borders the same day. The model replaces multi-bank correspondent chains with a single regulated rail, reducing the capital that has to be prefunded in each market and giving PPRO full visibility of every payment.
STARTING IN LATIN AMERICA
Latin America was the natural starting point. It is one of the fastest-growing regions for local payments, and one of the hardest for moving money out efficiently. By leveraging stablecoin rails, Damisa gives PPRO a faster and more predictable route to move its funds across Latin American markets.
Following the initial rollout, the partnership is now being extended to additional markets as PPRO grows its global footprint, with Damisa supporting collection, cross-border movement and local-currency settlement.
WHAT THEY SAID
“PPRO is one of the most respected names in local payments, having built their business on getting the local details right. We are proud to be the rail that makes their cross-border money movements faster and more efficient. Latin America was the proving ground: collect locally, move on stablecoin rails, settle in PPRO’s currency of choice the same day.”
Jordan Lawrence, CEO and Co-Founder, Damisa
“As we expand our platform globally, we continue to need fast and reliable ways to move funds across borders. Damisa gives us a regulated, stablecoin-powered solution that lets us settle in our currency of choice. The results in Latin America made the case for expanding it further.”
Almir Majcic, VP Treasury, PPRO
WHY STABLECOIN SETTLEMENT, AND WHY NOW?
Correspondent banking has been retreating from many of the corridors where cross-border demand is growing fastest, while regulation of stablecoins has matured through frameworks such as MiCA in the European Union and the GENIUS Act in the United States. Together, those shifts have made regulated stablecoin rails a credible settlement layer for institutional payment flows, not just for crypto-native businesses.
Damisa was built for that moment. It operates as a regulated, multi-jurisdiction platform, holding an Australian Financial Services License with AUSTRAC digital currency exchange and remittance registration, registration as a Money Services Business with FINTRAC in Canada, and a VASP registration in Poland, with Malta CASP and Payment Institution authorisation in progress. Sanctions, AML and transaction screening run on every payment. Damisa settled more than $70 million in the first half of 2026 across more than 90 countries and 70 currencies.

Spanish Banks Report 150% Spike in Fraud Conducted from Stolen Devices
summary:
Over the last 12 months, Spanish financial institutions have seen increases in attempted fraud sessions, attempted scam sessions, the average value of those fraud and scam attempts, and the number of digital banking sessions conducted from stolen devices. Stolen device fraud allows its perpetrators to profit twice: once by draining the victim’s bank account and a second time by selling the stolen device.
“In the first half of the year, our Spanish customers also reported a 35% increase in sessions involving malware,” BioCatch Director of Global Fraud Intelligence Thomas Peacock said. “That spike is consistent with the local increases we’ve seen in both job and investment scams, which often direct victims to install a bogus trading app or work portal that then infects the device with a piece of malware.”
Bad actors targeting the region increasingly impersonate legitimate institutions and the family members of their prospective victims, combining AI-generated voice cloning with live photo and video calls to build a convincing sense of legitimacy.
The Spanish banks reporting this data all work with BioCatch, which prevents fraud and scams by recognizing patterns in user behavior. Attempted fraud sessions at those banks increased by 19% over the last 12 months, attempted scam sessions by 46%, and the average value of a fraud attempt by 63%.
Other key report findings:
Scams most common fraud type: Social engineering scams accounted for 43% of all fraud and 60% of fraud losses in Spain over the last 12 months.
Bot sessions decline: As Spanish banks have improved their defenses against bots, fraudsters continue to pivot to social engineering attacks.
The report also includes a case study showing how behavioral intelligence identified a remote access attack on a corporate account.
